issues.description: The problem statement requires Bookstore to provide an initializer with the signature init(books: [Book]) (problem_statement.md lines 8-12). The reference Client implementation constructs a Bookstore using Bookstore(books: books) (Sources/BookstoreLib/Client.swift lines 31-58). However, the Bookstore implementation in the solution declares init() with no parameter and attempts to reference an undefined 'books' variable (Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift lines 9-16). This mismatch will cause compilation errors and prevents students from following the specified API.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Bookstore initializer to match the specified API and the client usage: implement init(books: [Book]) { self.books = books }. This makes the constructor signature consistent with the problem statement and with calls to Bookstore(books: books).

issues.description: The problem statement requires a Bookstore initializer with signature init(books: [Book]) and the Client constructs the bookstore with Bookstore(books: books), but the solution's Bookstore class defines init() with no parameter (and even references a nonexistent 'books' parameter inside). This creates a mismatched initializer name/parameter expectation across artifacts and will confuse students about which initializer to implement and use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Bookstore implementation match the problem statement and Client usage by changing the initializer to init(books: [Book]) { self.books = books }. Alternatively, if the design should use a parameterless init(), update the problem statement and all Client usages to call Bookstore() consistently — but prefer aligning the Bookstore initializer with init(books: [Book]).
